i0-context.title: Load baseline context
i0-context.imperative: Loaded: #511/#443 issues, Phase-C spec, archived #443 FINDINGS, physics packet map, LESSONS, the latitude contract. Grounded: MASS_KG=808 fixed constant in longitudinal_fit.py; physics pipeline quali-only; telemetry Parquet mirror has race sessions. Record pass.

w1-scope.title: W1 mass model — scope: produce-only vs rewire consumers?
w1-scope.imperative: Does W1 just PRODUCE m(lap) as a new module (and W2 consumes it), or also REWIRE the existing fixed MASS_KG=808 consumers (force_residual, braking_view, coast_view, decoupled_*) to take m(lap)? Recommend: produce-only new module this wave; rewiring is W2's concern when it actually fits race laps.
w1-scope.finding: DECISION: (b) produce + rewire all consumers. Mass model m(season,team,lap)=base_min(season)+team_offset(season,team)+fuel(lap). Per-season base; per-team overweight inflation hook (teams run over min). Constraint surfaced: MASS_KG=808 baked into theta_D=CdA/(2M) + 2023-Q pool comparability -> rewire must handle quali-reference preservation vs re-baseline.

w1-anchors.title: W1 anchor values — reg-min mass, fuel start, burn model
w1-anchors.imperative: Confirm anchors: reg-min car+driver mass per season (2023=798kg?), fuel start (full tank / race-distance x consumption; max 110kg reg), burn = pure linear (spec anchor). Edge: how m_dry relates to existing 808 ref (798 dry + ~10 nominal fuel?).
w1-anchors.finding: DECISION: per-circuit linear fuel (burn_per_lap x n_laps, cap 110kg); per-season reg base_min (798/798/798/800 verify). QUALI = base_min(season)+nominal_quali_fuel (~10kg, configurable) -> NOT a fixed cross-season 808; 2023 reproduces ~808 so 2023-Q pool preserved, 2025->~810. team_offset applies to quali+race, default 0.

w1-granularity.title: W1 granularity + SC/VSC/formation edge cases
w1-granularity.imperative: Per-lap fuel via race lap_number; how to handle SC/VSC (reduced burn), formation lap, red-flag restarts. Recommend: linear-by-racing-lap baseline, flag SC laps as a known approximation (intentional [IGNORE] per MODEL_SCOPE) unless evidence demands.
w1-granularity.finding: DECISION: (b) SC/VSC-aware cumulative burn (green laps full burn, SC/VSC reduced ~half). User: fuel est questionable regardless but SC-aware is trivial, eliminates one error source. DATA DEP: per-lap track-status (FastF1 TrackStatus) must be in the lap store; verify/ingest in W1.

w1-validation.title: W1 truth/validation — anchor or checked?
w1-validation.imperative: Fuel-mass is [MODEL/ANCHOR] (not fitted). Does W1 still validate (e.g. linear burn reproduces start-vs-end pace delta on a known race)? Recommend: light sanity check vs a known race fuel-effect (~0.03s/lap/10kg), but no fit.
w1-validation.finding: DECISION: (b) formula+bounds+physical sanity (mass-vs-lap curve, ~0.03 s/lap/kg gut-check, illustrative plot, no fit). FUTURE ISSUE (triage): file (c) full fuel-mass pace-validation under #509 (prove fuel correction flattens start-vs-end stint pace).

w2-fit-shape.title: W2 race-fit shape — per-lap / per-stint / stint-trajectory?
w2-fit-shape.imperative: The five-view estimator was built for ONE clean quali lap. On a race stint, tyre-age + fuel + track-evolution co-vary. What is a 'race fit' — per-lap fits (fuel-corrected via W1), per-stint aggregate, or a stint-trajectory fit with age as a covariate? This is the heart of W2.
w2-fit-shape.finding: DECISION: (B) per-stint decay fit, age covariate. User: must POOL MANY stints (single stint too thin). PRIOR ART reviewed = src/compound_prior 'Unified Tire-Wear Pipeline' (alternating pooled multi-race baseline+compound; per-compound beta/gamma; monotone+nonneg gamma; sparse prior; per-race delta-gamma; effective-age VSC/traffic modifier; identifiability.py encodes the pit-staggered levers same_progress_tire_age_spread/same_age_progress_spread/distinct_stint_start_bins + corr_tire_age_race_progress). Why it underperformed -> physics fixes: (1) race_progress fuel-proxy -> W1 real mass; (2) absolute C# -> relative-rank (#443); (3) lap-time response -> physics grip frontier; (4) separated tyre-vs-FUEL -> we separate tyre-vs-TRACK, same levers. DO NOT import compound_prior (evo region); use physics pooling.py + the regularizer as design template.

w2-views.title: W2 which views transfer to race laps?
w2-views.imperative: Race laps have traffic, dirty air, lift-and-coast, fuel-save — messier than quali flying laps. Which of the 5 views (braking/lateral/traction/powerdrag/coast) are reliable on race laps? #443 found lateral the clean grip instrument. Recommend lateral-first, characterize the rest.
w2-views.finding: DECISION: lateral-lead (clean deg instrument), traction-second (vector axis, peaks C4), braking+power-drag characterized (power-drag also = mass/fuel cross-ref), coast diagnostic-only. W2 produces all 5 so reliability is visible; tyre-age signal banked on lateral-first/traction-second per #443 + Piece-3 vector.

w2-lapselect.title: W2 lap selection / clean-air filter
w2-lapselect.imperative: Clean-air racing laps only? exclude in/out laps, SC/VSC, traffic (gap-ahead threshold), first lap. Reuse #443's committed-lap / clean-stint filters. Confirm filter definition.
w2-lapselect.finding: DECISION: reuse existing cleanliness filters - green-flag committed laps, exclude in/out/lap-1/SC/VSC/red-flag/invalid, configurable gap-ahead threshold (~1.5s) for dirty air (reuse regularizer close_ahead/cleanliness-tier + #443 committed-laps). Per-channel gap filtering (aero-sensitive stricter) deferred to diagnose-first if needed; start with one global threshold.

w2-output.title: W2 output/storage shape
w2-output.imperative: Produce per-(driver,race,lap-or-stint) FitRecord with tyre_life/compound/fuel/age attached, stored where? Extend estimate_store with race rows, or a new race-estimate store? Recommend extend with a session_type/race discriminator.
w2-output.finding: DECISION: (b) NEW race_stint_estimates table in the same store DB; per-(driver,race,stint) grain (stint_id, compound, tyre-age range, fuel/mass, g0+k per view, covariance blobs). Reuse EstimateStore plumbing (cov-blob encoding, _cov_list, read API) but distinct table for distinct grain (single canonical path, no quali-schema pollution; session_estimates @ estimate_store.py:335 untouched).

w2-coverage.title: W2 diagnose-first coverage gate
w2-coverage.imperative: First W2 gate evidence-only: how many 2023 races x drivers x clean stint-laps exist in the telemetry store; does a race lap even yield a stable five-view fit? Decide-fix the fit shape from this before freezing. Confirm diagnose-first.
w2-coverage.finding: DECISION: W2 opens with evidence-only diagnose-first gate (2023 first, extensible). Must establish: (1) coverage counts races x drivers x clean stint-laps, stints/compound; (2) per-stint five-view fit viability -> confirms (A) per-stint vs (B) joint fallback; (3) regularizer-style identifiability map (same_progress_tire_age_spread / same_age_progress_spread / distinct_stint_start_bins) -> are pit-staggered conditions present to separate tyre vs track in 2023. Ends at decide-fix checkpoint (lock fit shape + thresholds + supported circuits/compounds) before W2 freezes.

w3-separation.title: W3 tyre vs track separation method
w3-separation.imperative: mu_eff = mu_tyre(compound,age) x T_track(session). Issue: separate via pit-staggered fleet (diff ages/same time->pure tyre; same age/diff time->pure track) + #508 pooling. Confirm method; does the pooling machinery actually support within-race-time track-evolution, or is that net-new?
w3-separation.finding: DECISION: crossed fractional/log-grip model grip = car_envelope(driver,weekend) + f_tyre(compound,age) [season-pooled target] + g_track [weekend track-evolution nuisance] + noise. REFINEMENTS (user): (1) g_track is SESSION-AGNOSTIC / weekend-spanning - quali+practice also measure+feed it (quali = clean track probe); build interface right now (race+quali now, FP later #513). (2) Evolution axis = CUMULATIVE TRACK-LAPS run field-wide (rubbering proxy), NOT wall-clock (laps/min varies by session type). (3) car_envelope anchored from quali envelope (C1 #510). g_track per-(circuit,weekend) partial-pooled; f_tyre season-pooled via pooling.py; g_track within-weekend term likely NET-NEW. INTERFACE: W2 session-agnostic; race_stint_estimates carries session_type + cumulative_track_laps so FP/quali plug in w/o rework; FP FITTING stays #513. Gate build on W2 identifiability map.

w3-channel.title: W3 grip channel — scalar mu or per-axis vector?
w3-channel.imperative: #443/Piece-3: degradation is a VECTOR (lateral != longitudinal, decoupled on clean measures). Does W3 track per-axis grip-vs-age (lateral_mech/lateral_aero/traction) or a scalar mu_tyre? Recommend vector, lateral as the lead clean axis.
w3-channel.finding: DECISION: (a) per-axis vector f_tyre (lateral_mech/lateral_aero/traction), lateral-lead. User flagged 'it's a stretch' -> treat lateral as PRIMARY banked axis, traction as speculative second; per-axis honest-null OK (noisy traction vector = clean documented result, not failure). Keeps lateral<->braking conserved-budget trade as later diagnostic. Supplant test runs per-axis, expect win on lateral.

w3-supplant.title: W3 supplant test definition
w3-supplant.imperative: Define the incumbent precisely (current compound_adapter / lap-time compound estimation) and the metric (within-race pairwise ordering accuracy P per #443? plus magnitude R2?). The done-bar: physics mu(tyre-age) beats it. Confirm incumbent + metric.
w3-supplant.finding: DECISION (starting point, revisable at W2/W3 checkpoints per user): physics mu_tyre(age) vs incumbent set {absolute-C# floor, compound_prior gamma model} on within-race pairwise ordering accuracy P (held-out) + magnitude R2 + honest covariance overlap. #443 empirical telemetry sensor = independent CROSS-CHECK (not incumbent, not lap-time). Physics fit uses STRUCTURAL priors only (ordering/sign), NO #443 magnitudes (anti-circular). 2sigma = reference not gate (fine-margin, #512 precedent). Supplant judges DEGRADATION-ESTIMATION quality NOT finish-ranking (car-dominated, #443 POC; downstream lift = Phase-P #450). User expects learnings to reshape this.

w3-reachback.title: W3 reachback to C1 quali utilization
w3-reachback.imperative: #511 flags expected reachback: refine quali utilization (C1 #510) to race conditions once deg/fuel detangled. In scope for this epic or deferred to a #510 follow-on? Recommend: out of scope this epic, note the reachback on #510.
w3-reachback.finding: DECISION: defer race-utilization (C1 #510) refinement as NOT-REQUIRED but OPTIONAL/overridable - W3 commander may opt-in if the data breakdown looks useful (user: 'wouldn't be mad'). Note reachback as pick-up on #510 + #511. Rides as overridable pre-ruling/latitude in W3 launch order.

a443-deliverable.title: #443 arm — what it delivers this epic
a443-deliverable.imperative: Purpose here = the empirical cross-check / supplant incumbent for W3. Deliver: productionize the validated recipe (DRS-clean corner/straight contrast -> empirical mu(tyre-age) estimator + the within-race pairwise-P supplant harness)? Confirm.
a443-deliverable.finding: DECISION: (a) productionize the validated #443 recipe (DRS-clean corner/straight contrast, relative-rank, 2022+, committed-laps, mass-cancelled) = empirical mu_tyre(compound,age) estimator + shared within-race pairwise-P metric harness (NEUTRAL eval util, no physics->evo import). Telemetry-only, parallel with W2. EPIC-WIDE POSTURE (user): research-plan-for-improvement is a CLOSEOUT deliverable (first build = baseline not answer); every launch order explicitly tells agents to take NULL results in stride - baseline-first, stay confident/positive, don't overreact to negatives. Add to contract success-shape + comms + all launch-order inherited context.

a443-threads.title: #443 deferred threads — gate composition + new sensors
a443-threads.imperative: The two deferred #443 threads (per-regime gate composition; new sensors). In scope this epic, or just productionize the existing recipe as the cross-check and leave threads on #443? Recommend: productionize-only now; threads stay queued unless W3 needs them.
a443-threads.finding: DECISION: deferred #443 threads (per-regime gate composition; new sensors) -> closeout research-plan, stay tracked on #443, OUT OF SCOPE this epic (W3-triggered exception only if the comparison demands it). DEEP PRIORITY (user): build a SOLID EXPANDABLE BASE; user very likely to pivot to research immediately after -> expandability is a first-class design criterion across all waves (session-agnostic interface, injectable priors, vector channel, infra-reuse).

z-dashboard-verdict.title: Cross-cutting: dashboard + verdict bar
z-dashboard-verdict.imperative: Confirm the §4 done-done bar applies (coverage/honest-covariance/single-path/dashboard->verdict), one tyre-age characterization dashboard like #512's, GO/CONTEXTUAL/NO-GO verdict, 2sigma a reference not a gate (fine-margin per prior). Confirm.
z-dashboard-verdict.finding: DECISION: §4 done-done bar (coverage/honest-covariance/single-path/dashboard->verdict); one tyre-age characterization dashboard (coverage map, per-axis f_tyre(compound,age) ladders, g_track curves, supplant result, identifiability map); PER-AXIS verdicts GO/CONTEXTUAL/NO-GO (lateral expected strongest, traction may be CONTEXTUAL/NO-GO = fine); 2sigma reference not gate (#512). Same rigor/presentation as #512.

w1-team-inflation.title: W1 per-team mass-inflation hook design
w1-team-inflation.imperative: How is team_offset(season,team) sourced? Config anchor defaulting to 0 (settable from external knowledge), or estimable nuisance? Mass is [ANCHOR] not fitted -> lean config hook, default 0, door open. Confirm.
w1-team-inflation.finding: DECISION: (a) team_offset[(season,team)] config hook, default 0, anchor not fitted. FUTURE ISSUE (triage): estimation route (b) - estimate per-team mass offset from data.

w2-pooling.title: W2/W3 pooling architecture + boundary
w2-pooling.imperative: Pool many stints: per-stint-fit-then-pool (W2 produces per-stint grip-vs-age, W3 pools+separates) vs joint hierarchical multi-stint fit. Reuse regularizer identifiability levers on physics grip response + relative-rank + W1 fuel. Confirm split + approach.
w2-pooling.finding: DECISION: (A)-produces/(B)-separates split accepted as starting point + joint-fit fallback. SEASON POOLING design (user): COMPOUND = season-level strongly-pooled, highest-N axis (same compound x many races/circuits/drivers), should be the STRONGEST fit + strong informative prior (monotone-up ladder from #443+regularizer, gamma>=0, ranges) via the #496 injectable-(value,sigma) pattern. CIRCUIT = partial-pool, per-circuit heterogeneous nuisance (always a bit different, shrink-to-global w/ residual heterogeneity). + driver/car random effects. Use physics pooling.py random-effects+two-way. INTEGRITY CAVEAT: structural priors (ordering/sign) OK in the physics fit; #443 empirical MAGNITUDES stay OUT (else supplant test is circular) -> revisit at w3-supplant.

consolidation.verdict: Wave designs resolved for tire-age epic: W1 mass model (b-rewire, per-season base + per-team hook + per-circuit SC-aware fuel), W2 race-fit path (per-stint decay, session-agnostic interface, new race_stint_estimates table, diagnose-first opener), W3 separation (crossed fractional-grip car+f_tyre(compound,age,vector)+g_track(cumulative-laps,session-agnostic), season-pooled compound, supplant vs {absC#,compound_prior gamma}), #443 arm (productionize recipe + neutral pairwise-P harness, parallel W2). Posture: expandable base, null-in-stride, research-plan closeout deliverable.

triage_candidates.statement: Future issue under #509: full fuel-mass pace-validation (prove the fuel correction flattens start-vs-end stint pace on real stints; W1 shipped only formula+bounds+sanity).
Future issue under #509: estimate per-team mass offset (overweight cars) from data, vs the default-0 config anchor W1 ships.
